title: Article 387 — Special provision as to determination of population for certain transitional purposes (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 387 was a transitional provision for determination of population for certain purposes. Omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Spent; not living law.
content.glance: Art 387 omitted by 7th Amendment 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Transitional population determination — spent.
content.study: Part of the 379–391 transitional block. Omitted by 7th Amendment, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Status of Article 387?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Omitted by the 7th Amendment, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Spent transitional provision.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Article 387 was a transitional provision for determination of population for certain purposes. Omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Spent; not living law.

examples.title: Application of art-387
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the provision produce the consequence described in the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage art-387?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory or constitutional elements stated in the text.

distinctions.title: Scope of art-387
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the constitutional text.

misconceptions.myth: art-387 creates unlimited or extra-textual rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the constitutional provision.
